title: Exclusion, suspension and revocation lists set against the City ledger
question: Does the City pay any business that is on the federal exclusion list, the State Medi-Cal suspended list or the federal list of revoked Medicare enrolments?
finding: Of 3,546 businesses on the federal exclusion list, 1 carries the exact name of a City payee paid $10,000 or more; of 1,278 organizations on the State Medi-Cal suspended list, 0; of 5,130 organization entries on the federal revoked list, 4 payee names. 1 of these 5 name matches has a second key: Hometown Medical Supplies LLC (federal revoked medicare enrolments, San Jose, CA, from 2024-06-02; dme supplier - medical supply company: noncompliance (dme standards not met)) is City payee HOMETOWN MEDICAL SUPPLIES, paid $29,907 under fiscal-year labels 2017 to 2024. For the other 4 the records do not show whether it is the same organisation or two with the same name: Health Education Services (federal exclusion list, El Reno, OK, 1995-08-03) and City payee HEALTH EDUCATION SERVICES ($19,689, 2017 to 2025). The rest are national chains or universities with one store or clinic enrolment revoked. No City payment under a later fiscal-year label than the listing date is shown for any confirmed match.
how: Business names on the three lists were compared with every City payee paid $10,000 or more in the Controller's payment file, after removing punctuation and legal endings. A second key was then sought: the city the list gives (for the revoked list, the city where Medicare's supplier files place the listed provider number) against the cities in the payee's City business registration. The lists give no tax number, and the City payment file gives no provider number, so no exact identifier joins them. Individuals were not compared: a person's name alone identifies nobody.
limits: A shared name is not a match. Large pharmacy chains and universities appear because one of their many store or clinic enrolments was revoked for an equipment-supplier standard; that does not bar the company. The exclusion list reaches back decades and includes businesses long closed. The City may also pay a listed business for something other than health care, which the exclusion does not forbid unless federal health money pays for it.
